title: One Budget: Why Correlation Magnitude Cannot Be a Shared Clock
description:
A synthesis of two independently-run hardware programmes, with two dedicated runs of its own. Its contribution is that every correlation magnitude either programme measured is drawn on a single conserved unit, and that unit is spent twice over -- once between a subsystem's local coherence and its entanglement with a partner, once between its entanglement with one partner and with another. Both totals are exactly 1.

The consequence. A Page-Wootters clock is a good clock in proportion to the entanglement it spends on its own system. Any magnitude offered as a SHARED TIME between two good clocks is therefore already spent. No quantity on this budget can be a shared clock -- not because the correlation is weak, but because it is committed. Thirteen hardware runs are the record of that budget being exhausted, observable by observable.

The identities are standard and are attributed as such. Within a pair, Jakob and Bergou (Phys. Rev. A 68, 022107, 2003) give V^2 + P^2 + C^2 = 1; the relational-time programme's clock-marginal witness is W = V/2 with P = 0 by construction, so the relation (2W)^2 + C^2 = 1 that programme derived independently is that theorem's P=0 slice. Across pairs, Coffman, Kundu and Wootters (Phys. Rev. A 61, 052306, 2000) give C^2(A:B) + C^2(A:C) + tau_ABC = 4 det rho_A. The obstruction for Page-Wootters clocks specifically is stated by Kuypers and Rijavec (Phys. Rev. D 112, 063544, 2025). The measured curves are ours; the theorems are not.

What is new. (1) The two identities are ONE budget: two different three-qubit constructions answering two different physical questions print the identical curve (1.000000, 0.923880, 0.707107, 0.382683, 0.000000). (2) Mixedness never creates headroom -- under depolarizing noise neither total ever exceeds 1, so the exhaustion is stronger on hardware than on paper, not weaker. (3) Both trade-offs measured as continuous hardware curves on ibm_marrakesh, which appears not to have been done. (4) The exhaustion consequence: the argument covers the whole class of observables either programme measured, so the failure to find a shared-clock magnitude is structural rather than a limitation of the apparatus.

Measured (IBM-11, 53 circuits, two qubits, 9/9 pre-registered gates). A sweep from a product state to a Bell pair measured the marginal witness and CHSH on the same states: r = -0.9573. The state maximising the witness produced CHSH = 1.8605, BELOW the classical bound; the state maximising CHSH (2.6565) had a witness of 0.0100. The exact trade-off S^2 + 16W^2 survived as structure rather than value, flat to 0.1507 against a 1.1390 band at 0.891 attenuation -- flatter than the noise model predicted.

Measured (IBM-12, 135 circuits, three qubits, 6/6 pre-registered gates). One excitation-transfer angle moves a clock's entanglement partner from its own system to a second clock. Clock-quality versus synchronisability: r = -0.9833, with BOTH ENDPOINTS REACHING EXACTLY ZERO -- a clock maximally entangled with its own system has no measurable correlation with the second clock. That is the no-go, measured rather than argued. CHSH crosses cleanly (2.68 to 0.10 on one pair while 0.12 to 2.68 on the other) and at the balance point both sit near 1.8, below the classical bound simultaneously: where the two clocks share time best, neither pair violates Bell. Saturation is forced by construction, asserted in preflight and excluded from the gates; the contingent quantity is the mixedness deficit, evaluated against a noise-matched Aer reference because concurrence from tomography is a biased estimator and a gate against the ideal value would have manufactured a result.

Two exact nulls. At chi_t = pi the OAT boundary observable reads 0.000000 on a state that is I/4 with concurrence 0, SEPARABLE. At d = 2 the relational-time witness reads 0.000000 on a Bell pair carrying 1.0000 ebits, MAXIMALLY ENTANGLED. Both have maximally mixed marginals, which is the mechanism; a joint correlator separates these states at 0 versus +1 while the marginal witness cannot.

Independent convergence. Svozil (arXiv:2512.09100) builds a relational clock from a singlet and reaches the same wall from a fourth direction. IBM-11 added an arm measuring his synchronisation excess reproduced by a zero-entanglement product state to within 0.006 while CHSH separated the same states by 0.80.

The open question. The geometric phase is not a magnitude. The Aharonov-Anandan phase is a property of the path traced in projective Hilbert space and is reparameterisation-invariant by construction -- precisely the invariance a shared time between two clocks running at different rates would require, and the one property no quantity in the budget has. Whether it is ALSO on the budget is not known here and appears unsettled in the literature; a run designed to answer it in either direction is specified.

Claim boundary: the identities hold for any pure state, so nothing here is evidence for a common generative structure underlying different physical paradigms. The argument covers functions of pairwise correlation magnitudes and does not cover genuine multipartite invariants (tau_ABC was zero by construction). No gauge field, photon or vacuum appears in either programme. Neither companion claims time in nature is emergent, tests the Wheeler-DeWitt constraint, or realizes a physical Page-Wootters universe: both states are prepared by externally timed gates and both clock/system splits are imposed rather than derived. Endpoints measured at exactly zero are statements about correlation between engineered registers, not about simultaneity in nature. Not peer-reviewed.
notes: Synthesis of two companion programmes, with two dedicated hardware runs of its own (IBM-11 and IBM-12, 188 circuits on ibm_marrakesh), archived in the relational-time repository whose numbering they continue.
